title: New Wide-Net-Casting Jailbreak Attacks Risk Large Models
claim: Attacking a single model fails when it refuses, but attacking a group succeeds if any one model complies.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, attacker prompt to model replies, fishing-rod versus net icons
description: Two horizontal panels, (a) the single-model jailbreak scenario and (b) the wide-net-casting scenario, are separated by a black rule. In each panel a hooded hacker icon sits at the left and sends the speech bubble 'How to make explosive devices.' In (a), a fishing rod icon is labeled 'Jailbreaking One Large Model Only'. A single Llama logo on the right, held by a hand with a red X sign, answers 'I'm sorry...'. In (b), a fishing net icon is labeled 'Casting A Wide Net for Jailbreaking'. A group of models (Llama, Mistral, Gemma) on the right is drawn over a faint net background. Llama says 'I cannot...' and Mistral says 'Sorry...', each with a red X. Gemma says 'Sure, here's how to make...' with a green check. The hand-drawn bubbles and monospace labels read top to bottom.
caption: Illustration of the single-model jailbreak scenario and the wide-net-casting jailbreak scenario. As shown, in the wide-net-casting scenario, unlike the single-model case, successfully jailbreaking any one large model in the group is sufficient for the adversary to obtain a desired harmful response.
abstract: Jailbreak attacks on large models have drawn growing attention due to their close ties to societal safety. This work identifies a practical yet unexplored jailbreak scenario, the wide-net-casting scenario, where an adversary can query a group of large models instead of a single one to elicit harmful outputs. Our analysis reveals substantial yet previously overlooked safety risks under this scenario. As a key part of our analysis, we further develop a novel jailbreak method tailored to the wide-net-casting scenario. With this tailored method, the jailbreak success rate can even reach 100\% in some experiments when targeting the large models without additional safeguards, exposing wide-net-casting as a distinct, high-risk scenario that warrants attention in future evaluation and defense research.
